sender.en: A customer who shows you a “successful transfer” on their phone

name.en: Fake transfer alert: a buyer shows a payment screen or alert, but no money arrives

how.en: A buyer at your shop, stall, POS point or car lot pays “by transfer” and shows you a successful transfer screen or a credit alert. The screen comes from a doctored banking app or a “flash fund” app, so no money ever reaches your account. They blame network delays, take the goods or cash and leave. Traders in markets in Lagos, Benin City, Ogun and other states have lost goods this way.

text.en: A customer offers to pay by bank transfer and shows a successful transfer on their phone.
Your own account shows no credit, and they say it is network delay or the bank is slow.
They insist on taking the goods or cash now.
Oga I don send am, see the receipt for my phone. Na network dey delay the alert, e go soon enter. Abeg let me carry the goods, I get another place to rush to.

en: buyer showed transfer screenshot but no credit came
fake alert to buy goods from my shop
transfer successful on his phone but i was not credited
he said network will deliver the alert later
pos customer paid with fake transfer
alert did not reflect after he left with the goods
The payment screen is on their phone, not in your own bank app.
They say the alert is delayed by network or the bank.
They are in a hurry to leave with the goods or cash.
Only release goods or cash after the money shows in your own banking app or account statement, not on a text or a screenshot.
Ask your bank or POS provider to confirm a large payment before you hand over.
If it happened, report to the police and the NPF-NCCC with CCTV, the account name they showed and any phone number.
